text: Hi! I'm Leo. Are you new here?
Yes, I am. I'm Mia. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you, too. Where are you from?
I'm from Peru. And you?
I'm from Canada. Is this your first class?
Yes. Is this room three?
No, this is room two. Room three is next door.
Oh, thanks! See you there.
I'm Ana. Nice to meet you.
I'm from Peru. And you?
The class is next door.
Of course. Come with me.
Yes, she is. Her name is Anna.
Our teacher is Anna. Her surname is Reed.
Sorry, can you repeat that, please?
Reed. Anna Reed.
How do you spell Reed?
R, E, E, D. Do you have a pen?
Yes, I do. Is this her desk?
Yes. Put your name on this card, please.
OK. Mia. Is that right?
Can you repeat your name, please?
How do you spell Anna?
Room three. Is that right?
Yes. Write your first name here.
Yes, please. Your first name and your surname.
Come in! You can put your bag here.
Thanks. Under the table?
No, next to the chair. This is my brother, Ben.
Hi, Ben! Ella, is that his guitar?
Yes, it is. He plays every afternoon.
That's nice. Is your sister here too?
No, she's at school. Her name is Sara.
Oh, OK. Your house is really nice.
The bag is next to the chair.
This is my friend, Ana.
Is this your book?
It's upstairs, next to my room.
Of course. That chair is free.
What time do you finish school?
At three. I get home at half past three.
Do you do your homework in the afternoon?
Yes, I do. Then I play football.
I usually play the guitar after dinner.
Can we play together on Saturday?
Yes! I don't have a class on Saturday morning.
Great. Let's meet at ten.
What time do you get home?
I eat dinner. Then I read.
Let's meet at nine.
Yes, eleven is fine. See you then!
At my house. Bring your guitar!
Hi! What would you like?
I'd like a cheese sandwich, please.
Sure. Would you like a drink too?
Yes, a small tea, please.
With milk?
No milk, thanks. Do you have any water?
Yes. Still or sparkling?
Still, please. How much is it altogether?
I'd like a small coffee, please.
No sugar, thanks.
How much is the sandwich?
Of course. One apple juice.
No, but I can heat it for you.
Here's your sandwich and your tea.
Thank you. Sorry, where is my water?
Oh, sorry! Here it is.
Thanks. Can I pay by card?
Yes, of course. That's six pounds.
Here you are. Is this table free?
Yes. You can sit by the window too.
Great. Thank you for your help.
Your water? Here it is.
Can I pay in cash?
Is this chair free?
Of course. They're next to the till.
Yes. I'll put it in a bag.
Hello. Can I help you?
Yes, I'm looking for a jacket.
What colour would you like?
Blue, please. Do you have this one in small?
Yes. Here you are. You can try it on.
Thank you. Where are the changing rooms?
Over there, on the left.
Thanks. I'll try this one.
I'm looking for a blue shirt.
Do you have it in medium?
Can I try it on?
Yes, the green jackets are here.
It's twenty pounds.
How is the jacket?
It's a little small. Do you have a medium?
Yes. Try this one.
This is better. Is it warm?
Yes, it is. It's good for cold weather.
Good. It's cold outside today.
Yes, and rainy. Do you need an umbrella?
No, thanks. I have one. I'll take the jacket.
It's a little big.
The blue one is better.
I'll take this one.
Of course. It's on this label.
No problem. Let me know if you need help.
Hello. Do you need help?
Yes, please. Where is the bus stop for the museum?
It's across the street, next to the bank.
Thanks. Which bus do I take?
Number twelve. It stops outside the museum.
Is the museum far from here?
No. It's about ten minutes by bus.
Great. Number twelve, across the street. Thank you!
The bank is across the street.
Which train do I take?
It's about five minutes.
Yes. Go straight on and turn right at the park.
Yes. We're here, and the museum is here.
Good morning. Where are you going?
To the museum, please. One ticket.
That's two pounds.
Here you are. Is this seat free?
Yes. The museum is after the park.
Sorry, can you tell me when we get there?
Of course. Sit near the front.
Thank you. That's very kind.
Two tickets to the museum, please.
The bank is after the school.
Can you tell me the time?
Yes. The station is the last stop.
Yes. Put your card here, please.
Would you like to go to the park tomorrow?
Yes, I'd love to. In the morning?
Yes. Let's meet at nine.
Sorry, I have a class at nine. What about eleven?
Eleven is fine. Can you bring some water?
Of course. Are we meeting at the gate?
Yes, the gate next to the café.
Great. See you tomorrow!
Yes, I'd love to come.
What about Saturday?
See you at eleven!
Of course. Bring her with you!
Let's go to the café instead.
Did you have a good day yesterday?
Yes, I did. The park was great.
What did you do after lunch?
I visited my cousin. We watched a film.
Was the film good?
Yes, but it was very long. I was tired!
Did you get home late?
No, I got home at seven. What about you?
What did you do on Sunday?
We watched a short film.
I was happy yesterday.
Yes. The sandwiches were really good.
Good idea! Saturday is better for me.
How are you settling in? Have you unpacked everything yet?
Almost. I've put my clothes away, but my books are still in boxes.
There's some space on the shelf in the living room.
Thanks. Do you mind if I use the bottom shelf?
Not at all. What time do you usually leave for work?
At seven, but I'm working from home this week.
Good to know. I usually make breakfast at half past seven.
That's fine. We can share the kitchen then.
Have you finished your homework yet?
Do you mind if I open the window?
I'm studying at home this week.
Sure. They're in the cupboard above the sink.
I'd like that. I'll make some coffee.
You look a bit tired. Is everything OK?
Yes, but I couldn't study last night. The music was quite loud.
Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't realise you were working.
No problem. Could we keep it quiet after nine?
Of course. I'll use headphones in the evening.
Thanks. And I'll tell you when I have an important deadline.
That would help. Is Friday evening different?
Yes. I'm free then. We could watch a film together.
I didn't realise you were studying.
Could we clean the kitchen after dinner?
A short message would help.
Good idea. Then neither of us will forget.
OK. We can talk again next Sunday.
Are you still coming to the picnic on Saturday?
Yes! What should I bring?
We've got plenty of sandwiches, but we need something to drink.
I'll bring some juice and a few bottles of water.
Great. We're meeting by the lake at twelve.
What will we do if it rains?
We'll go to my flat. There's enough room for everyone.
OK. Send me a message if the meeting place changes.
What should I wear?
We need a few cups.
If it rains, we'll stay inside.
Not yet. Could you bring ten?
That would be lovely. A small one is enough.
Hi! We're at my flat now. It's raining quite hard.
Thanks for telling me. I'm sorry, but I'm going to be late.
That's OK. What happened?
My bus broke down. I'm waiting for the next one.
Do you know when you'll arrive?
Probably at half past twelve. Is that too late?
Not at all. We'll save you some food.
Thank you! I'll text you when I'm outside.
Thanks for letting me know.
I'm going to be about ten minutes late.
I'll call you when I arrive.
Of course. It's 18 Green Street, flat four.
Some ice would be useful, if you have time.
Can I help you?
Yes. My train to Oxford is delayed. Is there another one soon?
There's one at ten forty, but you have to change at Reading.
Is it faster than waiting for the direct train?
Yes, you'll arrive about half an hour earlier.
Can I use this ticket on that train?
Yes. Go to platform five and keep your ticket with you.
Thank you. Platform five, and I change at Reading.
We have to change at Central Station.
The train is faster than the bus.
Can I use this ticket tomorrow?
Fifteen minutes. The platforms are close together.
That's fine. Watch the screen for its new departure time.
Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
Yes, under Sam Torres. For two nights.
Here it is. A room on the first floor.
Is it facing the street? I'm a light sleeper.
Yes, but we have a quieter room at the back.
Could I have that room instead, please?
Of course. Here's your key. Breakfast starts at seven.
Thanks. Could you tell me where the lift is?
The booking is under Mia Cruz.
Do you have a larger room?
Could you tell me where breakfast is?
Yes, it's included in your booking.
Certainly. I'll bring one to your room.
Hi. What can I do for you?
I bought these headphones yesterday, but the left side doesn't work.
I'm sorry about that. Have you tried them on another device?
Yes, on my laptop. The same thing happens.
Do you have the receipt with you?
Yes, here it is. Could I exchange them?
Of course. I'll check if we have another pair.
Thank you. I'd like the same model if possible.
I tried again, but the same thing happens.
Could I exchange this one?
I'd like a blue pair, if possible.
Yes. We'll put it back on the card you used.
Certainly. Let's connect them to this phone.
First, turn on Bluetooth on your phone.
OK, it's on. What do I do next?
Hold this button until the light flashes blue.
Like this? I can see a blue light now.
That's right. Now select the headphones on your screen.
There are two names. Which one should I choose?
Choose the one ending in 24. Then play some music.
It works! Thanks for showing me.
What should I do first?
Wait until the light turns green.
Which button should I press?
Of course. This time, you press the buttons.
Go ahead. I'll wait here if you need me.
Welcome! Have you worked at an event before?
Only once. I helped at a school fair.
That's useful. Today you'll welcome people at the entrance.
Do I have to check their tickets?
Yes, and give them a map. You don't have to take any money.
OK. What should I do if someone needs help?
Call me on this radio. Please don't leave the entrance alone.
Understood. Could we test the radio now?
Do I have to wear this badge?
You don't have to bring food.
What should I do if the radio stops working?
Yes. Here's a short checklist.
Of course. Then you can try the next one.
Hi, Oliver. How is it going at the entrance?
Fine, but a visitor needs the quiet room. I'm not sure where it is.
It's on the ground floor, beside the office.
Could someone show her the way? I can't leave this desk.
Yes. I'll send Sam over in a minute.
Thanks. She's waiting by the blue chairs.
Got it. Please ask her to stay there.
I will. Thanks for your help.
I'm not sure which room it is.
Can you show them the way?
Got it. I'll wait here.
Yes. The quiet room is marked with a blue circle.
Ground floor, beside the office.
That photo is amazing. Where were you?
In the mountains last weekend. We were walking near a lake.
Did you walk all the way there?
Yes, but while we were taking photos, it started to rain.
Oh no! What did you do?
We found a small café and waited inside.
Was the trip disappointing after that?
Not really. We met two friendly hikers and shared our sandwiches.
While we were eating, the rain stopped.
What did you do next?
Was it difficult? Not really.
I'd love to see it. Was there a rainbow?
Good idea. And take a light raincoat!
Have you ever camped near that lake?
No, I haven't. I've only been there for the day.
I've camped twice, but never in the mountains.
Would you like to try it together in summer?
I'd love to. We'll need a tent and warm sleeping bags.
My cousin has a tent. I can ask to borrow it.
Great. Let's start with one night, not a whole week.
Agreed. We can make a list before we book anything.
Have you ever travelled alone?
I've only visited once.
Can I borrow your tent?
Yes. Nora knows the area well.
That sounds sensible for our first trip.
Have you had a chance to look at the project notes?
I've read them, but I'm not sure which part I'm responsible for.
You'll be collecting feedback from the people who use our website.
Right. Do you mean I should interview them or send a questionnaire?
Start with a short questionnaire. We can arrange interviews later.
That makes sense. How many responses are we hoping to get?
About twenty by Friday, if possible. Let me know if you need a hand.
Thanks. I'll draft the questions today and send them to you first.
Have you had a chance to check the timetable?
Do you mean we should contact everyone?
I might need a hand with the last section.
Of course. Here's the questionnaire we used last month.
Yes. Send it over before lunch and I'll take a look.
How's the questionnaire coming along?
I've finished a first draft, but two questions still sound confusing.
Let's have a look. What are you trying to find out here?
Whether people can find the contact page without asking for help.
Then why not ask them to try it and describe what happens?
Good point. That would give us more useful information.
Exactly. You can still ask how easy they found it afterwards.
I'll change those questions and test them with two people first.
How's your presentation coming along?
What are you trying to explain in this paragraph?
Good point. We should ask the visitors too.
Sure. I'll tell you if anything is still unclear.
Great. Then we can decide whether it needs more changes.
You look exhausted. What happened on the way here?
I was waiting on platform four when they announced a change.
Didn't the information screen show the new platform?
It did, but I was looking at my phone and missed it.
Oh no. So by the time you got there, the train had gone?
Exactly. Luckily, a member of staff helped me find another route.
Well, at least you're here now. Have you had anything to eat?
Not yet. A sandwich and five minutes to sit down would be lovely.
I was waiting for the bus when you called.
By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.
At least we have enough time for lunch.
Definitely. There's a bakery just around the corner.
Of course. I'll get us some water while you rest.
We probably haven't got time for the whole coastal walk now.
Could we do the shorter route and still see the lighthouse?
Yes, but we'd need to leave in the next ten minutes.
I'd prefer not to rush. What about taking the local bus there?
That's an option. If we catch the two o'clock bus, we'll have plenty of time.
Great. We could walk back along the beach if the weather stays dry.
And if it starts raining, we can get the bus back instead.
Perfect. Let's check the last bus before we set off.
I'd prefer not to drive at night.
What about visiting the museum first?
We should set off before it gets dark.
Sounds good. I'll check where the stop is.
That works for me. Tomorrow's forecast looks better anyway.
Have you worked at the returns desk before?
No, this is my first shift. Could you show me how it works?
First, each book is scanned. Then we check whether it's damaged.
And what should I do if a page is missing?
Put the book on this shelf and leave a note for the librarian.
Do I have to contact the person who borrowed it?
No, you don't have to. The librarian takes care of that.
Okay. I'll scan it, check it, and put any damaged books here.
Could you show me how to use the scanner?
You don't have to bring your own laptop.
Jo takes care of the bookings.
Of course. Start with this book and I'll help if you get stuck.
Absolutely. I'll wait while you make a note.
This book is wet. Was it like that when it was returned?
I don't think so. I checked it about half an hour ago.
Someone might have left the window open during the rain.
Maybe, but the books beside it are completely dry.
Good point. Could someone have spilled a drink on it?
There's an empty cup behind the shelf. That might explain it.
Let's tell the librarian what we've found without blaming anyone.
Agreed. We know the book is wet, but we don't know how it happened.
Someone might have moved the box.
The wrong address might explain it.
Let's discuss it without interrupting each other.
Thanks. I'll move the other books somewhere dry.
Yes. There may be a note at the front desk.
Hello, customer support. How can I help?
I'm calling about a lamp I ordered last week. It arrived with a broken base.
I'm sorry to hear that. Was the packaging damaged as well?
Yes, one corner of the box was torn. I've taken photos of both.
Could you email the photos with your order number?
Of course. I'd like a replacement if the same model is available.
It is. Once we receive the photos, we'll arrange collection and delivery.
Thanks. Could you confirm the dates by email so I can be at home?
I'm calling about my delivery.
I'd like a replacement for the damaged part.
Please send the details so I can check them.
Yes. Please include the new address in your email.
Yes. We can refund you once the damaged lamp is collected.
I'm following up on your replacement lamp. We can deliver on Tuesday.
Thanks for getting back to me. Unfortunately, I'll be away that day.
Would Wednesday morning be any better?
Yes, as long as the driver arrives before eleven.
I can't guarantee an exact time, but I can offer Thursday evening.
Thursday evening would be easier. Is there anything I need to prepare?
Please put the damaged lamp back in its box for collection.
No problem. So both the collection and the delivery are on Thursday?
Thanks for getting back to me so quickly.
I can come as long as we finish by six.
Is there anything I need to bring?
I'll send you a confirmation for six to eight in the evening.
Yes, an adult at the address can accept it and hand over the old lamp.
Did you see the message about the community centre closing?
I did, but I'm not sure whether it means permanently or just this weekend.
Alex said they were cancelling all the classes.
Did he hear that from the centre, or was he repeating someone else's message?
I don't know. The screenshot doesn't show a date.
Let's check the website before we tell anyone else.
Here it is: the building is closed on Saturday for repairs.
So the classes aren't ending. They're moving online for one day.
I'm not sure whether the meeting is online.
Alex said the class was starting later.
Let's confirm the time before we invite anyone else.
Good idea. He can correct the message in the group.
Yes. The notice doesn't list them individually.
My dad goes to the Saturday class. What should I tell him?
The building is closed for repairs, but his class will still take place online.
He hasn't used the video app before. Will someone help him?
According to the notice, students can join ten minutes early for technical help.
That's useful. Does he need to download anything?
It says he can use the link in his browser. I'll send him the instructions.
Could you explain that in a short message? Long instructions put him off.
Sure. I'll include the time, the link and where to get help.
The workshop will still take place on Monday.
According to the email, we need to arrive early.
The long queue put us off.
Thanks. A quick test call would help him feel more confident.
Good idea. They may already have a guide for new users.
Have you seen anything we could watch together on Friday?
I watched a comedy about two neighbours who accidentally swap dogs.
That sounds silly. Was it actually any good?
Better than I expected. The story was simple, but the characters felt believable.
Would Jamie enjoy it? He usually prefers something with a bit of mystery.
There is a small mystery, although it's easy to guess the ending.
As long as it's not too long, I'm happy to give it a try.
It's about ninety minutes. Shall I send everyone the trailer first?
The exhibition was better than I expected.
I enjoyed it, although the beginning was slow.
We could give the new café a try.
Good plan. I'll find a second option with more mystery.
Okay. I'll mention the length and ask if anyone has seen it.
That went well. Everyone seemed to enjoy themselves.
Yes, although I spent more time preparing food than watching the film.
I hadn't realised. We should have helped you more.
Next time, would you mind asking everyone to bring something?
Not at all. We could make a list so we don't end up with five bags of crisps.
And maybe we could choose the film a few days earlier.
Agreed. If we share the jobs, it'll be easier for everyone.
Great. I'll host again if someone else takes care of the food.
I hadn't realised you were doing all the work.
Would you mind bringing some plates?
We ended up with too much food.
Perfect. I'll take drinks and help tidy up afterwards.
I'd like that. We can each bring our own lunch.
The client has asked whether we could bring the launch forward by a week.
We could, provided we reduce the scope. The payment feature still needs testing.
I was hoping we'd have everything ready by then. What's the main obstacle?
It's not the design itself; it's making sure the payment process works reliably.
Would bringing in another developer make enough of a difference?
Possibly, but getting someone up to speed would take a few days.
So what would you be comfortable committing to by the earlier date?
The information pages and booking form, with payments added the following week.
We can accept, provided we receive the data today.
I'll get the new designer up to speed tomorrow.
We're committing to delivering a tested version.
Yes. Include what each option would mean for users.
Absolutely. I'd rather give a realistic date than revise it later.
I've told the client that users will be able to pay on launch day.
Sorry, I think we may have been talking at cross purposes.
I thought you said the booking form would be ready.
It will, but it only collects requests. It won't process payments yet.
Right, I see the distinction now. We need to correct the message quickly.
Agreed. Could we explain that bookings will be confirmed manually for the first week?
Yes, and I'll make sure the support team knows what to tell customers.
Thanks. I'll add that limitation to the launch notes so it's clear to everyone.
We were talking at cross purposes about the deadline.
I see the distinction between a request and a confirmed booking.
I'll make sure everyone receives the update.
Good idea. That way we can check the wording against the actual feature.
Thanks. Please copy me in so we have the same record.
I still can't believe we booked the hotel for the wrong month.
I must have selected November instead of October without noticing.
Didn't the confirmation show the dates clearly?
It did. If I'd checked it properly, we'd have spotted the mistake straight away.
We both should have checked. I only looked at the price and the address.
At least the receptionist managed to find us a room nearby.
True, although it cost more than we'd budgeted for.
Next time, let's read the details out loud before either of us confirms.
I must have left the charger in the room.
If I'd checked the map, I wouldn't have missed the turn.
We hadn't budgeted for an extra night.
Let's keep future bookings in one shared folder.
That's true. The mistake was expensive, but the place is lovely.
Can we talk about the extra hotel charge before we leave?
Of course. I paid it at the desk, but I wasn't sure how we should split it.
Since I made the booking, I feel I ought to cover more of it.
I appreciate that, but we agreed on the booking together. Half each seems fair.
Are you sure? I don't want you to feel stuck with my mistake.
I'm sure. I'd rather sort it out now than let it become awkward.
All right. Send me the amount and I'll transfer my half tonight.
Thanks. Once that's done, let's put it behind us and enjoy the last day.
I feel I ought to apologise.
Let's sort it out before the next meeting.
We've agreed on a solution. Let's put it behind us.
Thanks. I'll send you a photo of the receipt.
That's fine. Just let me know which days work for you.
This report claims the training doubled staff productivity. Impressive, isn't it?
It sounds promising, but I'd like to know what they measured.
The chart shows that people completed twice as many tasks afterwards.
Were they the same type of tasks, and did the quality stay the same?
The summary doesn't say. It also doesn't mention how many people took part.
Then we should be cautious about applying the result to our whole team.
Fair enough. The training may have helped, but this alone doesn't prove it caused the change.
Exactly. Let's ask for the full method before making a recommendation.
I'd like to know what the results actually show.
We should be cautious about comparing such different groups.
This alone doesn't prove the new system is better.
Yes, as long as we also check quality and staff feedback.
Good point. New software might have affected the results too.
Can you give me the short version? Should we buy the training or not?
The results are encouraging, but the evidence isn't strong enough for a company-wide purchase yet.
What's the biggest gap in the report?
We don't know whether the tasks were comparable before and after the training.
So you're not saying the course doesn't work?
No. I'm saying we can't tell how much of the improvement came from the course itself.
What would you recommend as a next step?
Ask for the missing details, then consider a small pilot with clear success criteria.
Here's the short version of the proposal.
I'm saying we can't tell which option is cheaper yet.
As a next step, we should speak to the users.
Please do. Include the cost, the timeframe and what we'd measure.
That seems reasonable. Could you contact them today?
I like the idea of a garden, but who's going to look after it once the excitement wears off?
That's a fair concern. We're proposing a rota, with a named coordinator each month.
And what about noise? My windows face the site.
We'd keep activities within agreed hours. There wouldn't be evening events during the week.
I suppose that would help. Who would deal with complaints if the rules weren't followed?
The coordinator would be the first contact, and the council would review any ongoing issues.
I'd be more comfortable if those commitments were included in the proposal.
Absolutely. Would you be willing to read that section before we submit it?
That's a fair concern. We need a backup plan.
I'd be more comfortable if the costs were clearer.
Would you be willing to join a short meeting?
That would address my main worries. I'd be happy to review it.
A trial sounds sensible, provided residents can give feedback.
Some residents want a quiet garden, whereas others want a space for workshops.
Those aims aren't necessarily incompatible. Could we separate the areas?
The site isn't very large. Physical separation might not solve the noise problem.
Then perhaps we could separate activities by time rather than by space.
You mean quiet use most of the week, with scheduled workshops at weekends?
Exactly, with limits on group size and enough notice for neighbours.
That seems like a workable compromise, assuming we can manage the bookings.
Let's try a simple calendar first and review whether it works after a month.
Some prefer mornings, whereas others can only come at night.
More expensive doesn't necessarily mean better.
A shared schedule could be a workable compromise.
Great. We can show residents exactly what we're proposing.
Good idea. We shouldn't assume everyone's routine is the same.
Thank you for contacting us. Could you tell me what happened on the tour?
The description said the route was step-free, yet two stops could only be reached by stairs.
I'm sorry. Were alternative arrangements offered by the guide?
Only at the second stop. My mother had to wait outside during the first one.
I understand why that was disappointing. The route was changed recently.
That may explain it, but the booking page should have reflected the change.
You're right. I'll ask the team to correct it and review your booking.
Thank you. I'd appreciate a written response explaining what remedy you can offer.
The venue looked small, yet it felt welcoming.
The email should have mentioned the change.
I'd appreciate a written response by Friday.
I'll ask our manager to consider that and reply within three working days.
Understood. I'll send you the updated description once it's been checked.
Are you still planning to leave a review of the tour?
Yes, but I want to include how they handled the complaint as well.
Did they offer anything beyond an apology?
They gave us a partial refund and updated the accessibility information.
That sounds fair. Will you recommend the tour now?
With reservations. The guide was excellent, but visitors should check the current route carefully.
So you'd distinguish the quality of the guide from the booking information?
Exactly. A useful review should explain who the experience would suit and why.
They offered support beyond an apology.
I'd recommend it, but with reservations.
We should distinguish the service from the location.
That seems balanced. Readers can decide whether it suits them.
Good idea. That keeps the whole story in one place.
Honestly, I think language classes are a waste of time. You learn more from watching series.
I can see why you'd say that if your classes were mostly worksheets.
Exactly. I barely got to speak, whereas series exposed me to real conversations.
That helped me too. Still, understanding a scene isn't quite the same as responding in one.
Fair point. I sometimes know what I want to say but can't get it out quickly.
For me, the useful part is combining listening with practice that makes me retrieve the language.
So it's less about choosing one method and more about how you use it?
That's how I see it. I'd keep the series and add short conversations with feedback.
I can see why you'd say that after your experience.
Recognising a word isn't quite the same as using it.
That's how I see it, though my experience may be different.
Retelling a short scene, then trying it again without the script.
